module_title: Human Physiology II: Excretory, Skeletal, Neural & Endocrine Anatomy
introduction: This foundational level introduces the structural frameworks for waste elimination (Excretory), bodily movement (Locomotion & Skeletal), electrical communication (Neural), and chemical signaling (Endocrine). Mastering the exact anatomical locations and basic classifications of these systems is the first step.

core_concepts.title: Modes of Excretion & Human Excretory System
core_concepts.description:
Animals eliminate nitrogenous wastes in three main forms:
1. Ammonotelic: Excrete Ammonia (highly toxic, requires massive water). Bony fishes, aquatic amphibians, aquatic insects.
2. Ureotelic: Excrete Urea (less toxic). Mammals (including humans), terrestrial amphibians, marine fishes.
3. Uricotelic: Excrete Uric Acid (least toxic, requires minimum water, excreted as paste/pellet). Birds, reptiles, insects, land snails.
Human Excretory System: Consists of a pair of kidneys, one pair of ureters, a urinary bladder, and a urethra. The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the **Nephron**.

core_concepts.title: Locomotion & The Skeletal System
core_concepts.description:
Human skeletal system consists of 206 bones.
1. Axial Skeleton (80 bones): Skull (22 bones: 8 cranial, 14 facial), Hyoid bone (1, U-shaped at base of buccal cavity), Ear ossicles (6: Malleus, Incus, Stapes), Vertebral column (26: Cervical-7, Thoracic-12, Lumbar-5, Sacral-1 fused, Coccygeal-1 fused), Sternum (1), Ribs (12 pairs: 1-7 true, 8-10 false/vertebrochondral, 11-12 floating).
2. Appendicular Skeleton (126 bones): Limbs (Forelimbs 30 $\times$ 2 = 60, Hindlimbs 30 $\times$ 2 = 60) and Girdles (Pectoral/Shoulder girdle = 4 bones, Pelvic/Hip girdle = 2 bones).

core_concepts.title: Neural System Anatomy
core_concepts.description:
The Neural system coordinates and integrates all activities. The structural and functional unit is the **Neuron** (composed of Dendrites, Cell body/Soma containing Nissl's granules, and an Axon ending in synaptic knobs).
Human Neural System is divided into:
1. CNS (Central Nervous System): Brain and Spinal Cord. The site of information processing and control.
2. PNS (Peripheral Nervous System): All nerves leaving the CNS (Cranial and Spinal nerves). Divided into Somatic Neural System (relays impulses to skeletal muscles) and Autonomic Neural System (ANS, relays impulses to smooth muscles and involuntary organs, further divided into Sympathetic and Parasympathetic).

core_concepts.title: Endocrine Glands & Hormones
core_concepts.description:
Endocrine glands lack ducts (ductless glands) and release their secretions called **Hormones** directly into the blood. 
Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts. 
Major Glands: Hypothalamus (basal part of diencephalon), Pituitary (master gland in sella turcica), Pineal (dorsal side of forebrain), Thyroid (neck), Parathyroid (back of thyroid), Thymus (between lungs), Adrenal (top of kidneys), Pancreas (composite gland), Gonads (Testis/Ovary).

important_entities.name: Types of Joints
important_entities.key_fact: Classified into Fibrous, Cartilaginous, and Synovial.
important_entities.significance:
1. Fibrous: Do not allow any movement (e.g., Sutures in the skull). 
2. Cartilaginous: Allow limited movement (e.g., between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column). 
3. Synovial: Characterized by a fluid-filled synovial cavity, allowing considerable movement (e.g., Ball and socket joint - shoulder; Hinge joint - knee; Pivot joint - atlas/axis; Gliding joint - carpals; Saddle joint - carpal/metacarpal of thumb).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume floating ribs (11th and 12th pairs) are completely free. This is false. They are called 'floating' only because they do not attach ventrally to the Sternum. They are still firmly attached DORSALLY to the thoracic vertebrae.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: From outer to inner ear: **M**alleus (hammer-shaped, attached to tympanic membrane), **I**ncus (anvil-shaped), **S**tapes (stirrup-shaped, attached to the oval window of the cochlea). Stapes is the smallest bone in the human body.

exam_strategy_tips: Always differentiate between True ribs (1-7, attach directly to sternum via hyaline cartilage) and False ribs (8, 9, 10). False ribs do not articulate directly with the sternum; instead, they join the 7th rib using hyaline cartilage.
